findings.source_quote: the years following are known as A.D. (Anno Domini, Latin for “The year of our Lord”)
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the explanatory phrase into Kiswahili, for example: “B.K. (Anno Domini, Kilatini kwa ‘Mwaka wa Bwana wetu’).”
findings.translation_quote: miaka inayofuata hujulikana kama B.K. (Anno Domini, Kilatini cha “Mwaka wa Bwana wetu”)

findings.location: HTML, hymn beginning “What child is this”
findings.source_quote: Whom angels greet with anthems sweet, / While shepherds watch are keeping?
findings.suggested_fix: Revise these lines to retain the source’s meaning, for example: “Ambaye malaika humsalimu kwa nyimbo tamu, / Wachungaji wakiendelea kulinda?”
findings.translation_quote: Ambaye malaika humsalimu kwa nyimbo tamu, / Wachungaji wakilinda na kutazama?

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “The sign of the manger”
findings.source_quote: The sign of the manger in conjunction with their scriptural knowledge of Bethlehem were all that was needed for the shepherds to find the child.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the claim that the manger sign and their scriptural knowledge together were all they needed, for example: “Ishara ya hori, pamoja na ujuzi wao wa Maandiko kuhusu Bethlehemu, vilikuwa vyote walivyohitaji wachungaji ili kumpata mtoto.”
findings.translation_quote: Ishara ya hori, pamoja na ujuzi wao wa Maandiko kuhusu Bethlehemu, vilitosha kuwasaidia wachungaji kumpata mtoto.

findings.source_quote: This is the difference between nominal worship and the heartfelt praise of His redeemed who will but follow Him to the manger.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate “who will but follow Him” as a call to follow him, rather than implying that they will follow him only as far as the manger; for example: “Hii ndiyo tofauti kati ya ibada ya jina tu na sifa za moyoni za waliokombolewa naye, ambao watamfuata hadi horini.”
findings.translation_quote: Hii ndiyo tofauti kati ya ibada ya jina tu na sifa za moyoni za waliokombolewa naye, ambao watamfuata tu hadi horini.

findings.source_quote: Good Christians, fear, for sinners here / The silent Word is pleading.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the address to Christians and the reason for fearing, without changing the line into a command to be afraid: “Wakristo wema, ogopeni, kwa maana hapa Neno kimya linawaombea wenye dhambi.”
findings.translation_quote: Wakristo wema, ogopeni, maana kwa wenye dhambi hapa / Neno kimya linaomba.

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “These are those who are at peace”
findings.source_quote: They are content with a cottage while others cloister in a castle.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the contrast as being content with a cottage while others live in a castle, not as being confined there; for example: “Wanatosheka na nyumba ndogo huku wengine wakiishi katika kasri.”
findings.translation_quote: Wanatosheka na nyumba ndogo huku wengine wakiishi kifungoni ndani ya kasri.

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “Those whose hearts resound”
findings.source_quote: This is the song that Stephen sang proceeding his earthly departure. He spake of Abraham removing himself from his land, Acts 7:3 of Joseph being sold out of his home, vs.9 and of Moses being cast out, and fleeing to Midian. vs.21.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the factual change about Joseph: the source says he was sold from his home, not sold out of his home. For example: “...kuhusu Yusufu kuuzwa akiwa mbali na nyumbani, mst. 9...”
findings.translation_quote: ...kuhusu Yusufu kuuzwa kutoka nyumbani kwake, mst. 9...

findings.suggested_fix: Retain the source’s “outside” sense without implying movement into the group; for example: “Nje ya Kundi la Nyumba ya Wageni.”
findings.translation_quote: Nje ya Kundi la Nyumba ya Wageni
